Switched to an off-heat poach: bring to a boil, then turn off the heat and cover. Pull at 160°F (it coasts to 165°F while resting); before, it simmered 12–15 minutes to 165°F. Added a step to pound breasts to an even thickness and a 10-minute rest in the liquid for shredding. Total time 25 → 35 min.
why: Gentler cooking keeps the chicken juicier and avoids the rubbery texture of overcooking.

Heating the oven is now its own first step, and the steps say when the pan goes in and comes out. Garlic, rosemary and Parmesan moved from before roasting to after the flip. Pan is oiled before smashing; potatoes are no longer tossed by hand.
why: The oven timing was easy to miss, and garlic and cheese could burn over nearly 30 minutes at 425°F. Tossing by hand broke the smashed potatoes.

summary: Added an oven preheat to 400°F at step 2 (it was missing). The broil step now says to switch the oven to broil and use the top third of the oven.
why: The oven was never preheated, and the broil step was vague.

summary: The oven preheat to 450°F moved to the final rise, about 30 minutes before it ends. Before, it came right before baking.
why: A 450°F oven needs 20–30 minutes to heat, so the bread would have gone into a cold oven.

summary: Heating the oven is now its own step, and the tofu is seasoned while it heats. The toss step says to take the pan out and return it.
why: The tofu went into the oven before it had time to heat.

summary: The oven preheat moved from the rice step to the mushroom step. The bake step now says to put the pot or dish in the oven uncovered.
why: The oven was heating about 45 minutes before it was needed, and the bake step didn't say what goes in.

summary: The oven now starts heating with 15 minutes of marinating left (before, it started after). The glaze step says to take the pan out and return it.
why: The salmon would otherwise wait 15 minutes for the oven.

summary: The roast and flip steps now say when the pan goes in and comes out of the oven.
why: Small gaps in the oven instructions.

summary: Added the change log: changelog.json as the source of truth, a Change log page and per-recipe History section in the book, and CHANGELOG.md generated for GitHub.

Added four color themes, picked from the dots next to Change log: Sage (the original), Dusty Rose, Terracotta, and Black & White. Each one follows the device's light/dark setting, and the choice is saved per device.
why: Lets each person pick the look they like while keeping the book simple.

summary: Split the change log in two. The book's Change log page and CHANGELOG.md now show recipe changes only; system changes (themes, icons, layout, features) go to SYSTEM-CHANGES.md, with the files touched and a link to each commit.
why: Cooks only need recipe history; system changes are for the admin.
